A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, renamed from CellFlow to CellFlux. The main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on BBBC021, RxRx1 and JUMP, including baseline comparisons, ablations, held-out perturbation results and generated-image analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds sample-size tests, a MorphoDiff comparison, cross-dataset generation examples and CellProfiler measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same conditional flow matching, U-Net, noise augmentation, classifier-free guidance and ODE inference procedure. The renaming does not change the method; Appendix J's suggested latent-space interpolation and additional losses are future proposals.

E1.justification: The three datasets and primary perturbation tasks remain. Appendix H adds a limited qualitative transfer scenario: a BBBC021-trained model applies AZ138 and demecolcine perturbations to RxRx1 and JUMP control images, although those target datasets lack corresponding perturbed images.

E2.justification: PhenDiff and IMPA remain the principal evaluated baselines. MorphoDiff, previously included only in related work, becomes an evaluated BBBC021 comparator in v2 Table 6, with image-quality and MoA scores.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation through macro/weighted MoA F1, MoA assessment of OOD and batch-effect conditions, sample-size sweeps, cross-dataset testing and CellProfiler nuclear-size measurements. Section 4.1 also corrects the stated RxRx1/JUMP channel counts from 5/6 to 6/5; this reporting correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds tests of whether FID/KID advantages persist across sample sizes, qualitative robustness to cross-dataset shift, and preservation of perturbation-induced nuclear-size changes. These extend the existing component ablations, batch-effect analysis and trajectory examples, which remain.

E5.justification: v2 Table 7 introduces means with 95% confidence intervals for nuclear-size measurements; v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. Neither version specifies repeated training runs or seeds, and the added intervals do not establish additional model runs.

E6.justification: The principal Table 1 and per-perturbation Table 4 scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial F1, OOD MoA, sensitivity, MorphoDiff, nuclear-size and transfer results. It also revises other-batch initialization FIDo/FIDc from 23.7/71.9 in v1 Table 2d to 19.9/66.3 in v2 Table 2c, without explaining the numerical revision.

T1.justification: The graphical model, Proposition 1, KL-divergence comparison and conditional-mutual-information proof in Appendix A are unchanged. The flow-matching equations and mathematical assumptions are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: distribution-to-distribution morphology prediction, batch-effect handling and cellular-state interpolation. The headline 35% FID improvement and 12% MoA accuracy improvement remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The revised Impact Statement and new Appendix J explicitly acknowledge that interpolated states lack biological validation, identify possible pixel-space shortest-path artifacts, and propose validation strategies. Appendix H additionally interprets qualitative transfer as suggesting foundation-model potential while acknowledging unavailable target images.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-page access information in the abstract and identifies CellProfiler for the new morphology analysis. Appendix C's architecture, perturbation embeddings, optimizer, hyperparameters, hardware and training times remain unchanged; the PDF alone does not establish what resources the project page provides.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zheng et al.'s Guided Flows citation and an Appendix H explanation of baseline selection. IMPA and MorphoDiff publication updates refer to previously cited works, and the main positioning against existing generative approaches remains.

P1.justification: The paper is renamed CellFlux, publication information and acknowledgments are added, and results passages and the Impact Statement receive localized revisions. Appendix J is added, but most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 changes from four compact panels to stacked, expanded tables with additional metric columns and reference entries. v2 adds Tables 5–7 and Figure 11 and rearranges appendix layouts. The earlier related-work Table 5 survives as Table 8; existing qualitative and trajectory images are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity tests, baseline comparison and morphology measurements strengthen validation beyond v1's evidence, while Appendix J makes the trajectory-validation limitation explicit. These are useful but limited gains: cross-dataset transfer remains qualitative without target images, and the new nuclear-enlargement description of demecolcine is not reconciled with the retained smaller-nuclei descriptions.
